title: VPC connection latency thresholds and fallback orchestration guide
author: Amelia Park
body:
Overview:

This guide defines latency-related thresholds and an automated fallback orchestration pattern for VPC private deployments. It targets customers who use Redwood Private (VPC mode) and run inference traffic through the redwood-control-plane proxy into a tenant-local redwood-runtime fleet. The goal is to keep customer applications available with predictable degradation while minimizing model-quality regressions and unit-cost spikes during network anomalies or regional link issues.

Scope:
- Applies to: VPC-connected private deployments where the control plane and compute may be separated by WAN links (regional control plane, local runtime).
- Not covered: Full air-gapped single-site installs (see onprem packaging docs) and edge-only micro-appliances.

Audience:
- Field operators and SREs (primary)
- Customer platform engineers (secondary)
- Product and solutions engineers implementing SLAs and handoffs

Definitions:
- control-plane-proxy: The small in-customer proxy that terminates client TLS and forwards requests to redwood-control-plane services.
- redwood-runtime: Inference worker fleet (GPU-backed) running model shards/serving runtime.
- routing-orchestrator: Service responsible for applying routing policies and activating fallbacks (could be hosted in the control plane or deployed as a customer operator).
- KV-cache warm: Process of populating local per-model key-value caches to avoid cold-token penalties on failover.

Architecture sketch (textual):
- Clients -> customer VPC ingress -> control-plane-proxy -> redwood-control-plane (policy + routing) -> routing-orchestrator -> redwood-runtime clusters (primary regional).
- Optional: local standby runtime cluster in-customer that can serve a subset of models for degraded operation.

Operational SLOs and thresholds (summary table):

Action Threshold (value) | Triggered action
--- | ---
Control plane RTT (p95) > 200ms for 60s | Start degraded routing evaluation (stage 1)
Control plane RTT (p99) > 350ms for 30s | Initiate immediate lightweight fallback (stage 2)
Client-observed token latency increase > 2x baseline P50 for 2 successive minutes | Flag request-level degradation and consider per-tenant throttles
Loss of 30%+ control-plane requests (5m) | Promote local standby or regional fallback (stage 3)
Model cache hit-rate drop > 25% with rising latency | Delay full model swap; prefer prefix-preserving fallbacks

Note: thresholds above are defaults. Customers may tune per-tenant in the routing policy. All thresholds are expressed in wall-clock time averaged windows and must be evaluated with smoothing windows to avoid oscillation.

Trigger matrix (detailed):
- Stage 0 (healthy): p95 RTT < 150ms, p99 < 250ms, cache hit-rate > 90%. No action.
- Stage 1 (watch): p95 RTT 150–200ms or p99 250–350ms for 60s. Notify SRE and begin KV-cache pre-warm for candidates.
- Stage 2 (degrade): p99 RTT > 350ms or client token latency 2x baseline. Activate degraded routing: prefer local standby or smaller models, enable reduced-compute variants (quantized) for non-critical routes.
- Stage 3 (failover): sustained request failures or >30% packet loss over 5m. Shift traffic to local standby or remote-region regional-fallback topology; engage customer NOC and escalate to oncall.

Orchestration procedures (automated path):
1) Detection and stabilization (automated):
   1.1) routing-orchestrator consumes telemetry from redwood-control-plane metrics (control_plane_rtt_p95/p99, egress_error_rate, cache_hit_rate).
   1.2) Apply smoothing: 60s exponential smoothing with alpha=0.3 for RTT metrics.
   1.3) If Stage 1 conditions are met, automatically trigger KV-cache pre-warm for top-5 models for the tenant.

2) KV-cache pre-warm recipe (operator):
   - Select top-5 models by request volume from last 24h (fallback to tenant config).
   - Execute small synthetic prefix warm-up requests against local runtime:
     curl -s -X POST https://local-runtime.example.internal/v1/generate 
       -H 'Authorization: Bearer $LOCAL_OP_TOKEN' 
       -d '{"model":"<model-id>","prompt":"Warmup: hello","max_tokens":16}'
   - Monitor cache_hit_rate. Proceed to 2nd step when cache_hit_rate > 60% for warmed models.

3) Degraded routing activation (automated or manual):
   3.1) Update routing policy to prefer local standby or quantized model variants for non-SLA-critical routes.
   3.2) Apply per-route rate limits: reduce burst tokens by 30% for non-essential routes.
   3.3) Emit event to ticketing system with tags: [vpc-degrade][tenant:<id>][stage:2].

4) Model refresh / rolling swap while degraded (safe pattern):
   4.1) Do not perform full model swaps during stage 2 unless explicitly required by correctness regressions.
   4.2) If model refresh is required (patched model weights), use a 3-wave canary:
       - Wave A: 1% of traffic to refreshed variant on isolated nodes with KV-cache pre-warm. Run automatic quality checks (LLM eval set, latency + token-cost checks).
       - Wave B: 10% of traffic after 15 minutes if Wave A passes.
       - Wave C: 100% after 1 hour and satisfactory telemetry.
   4.3) If any wave fails quality or latency gates, rollback to previous variant and annotate the rollback event.

5) Failover to regional fallback (Stage 3):
   5.1) Only after KV-cache warm attempts and degraded routing did not restore acceptable latency.
   5.2) Configure sticky routing: keep in-flight request affinity to avoid request-level duplication.
   5.3) Activate regional-fallback routing policy: route traffic to the next-best region (e.g., us-east-2) with explicit customer SLA acceptance for increased latency.
   5.4) If the customer maintains a local standby, promote it from standby to active and scale pods with conservative autoscale policy (scale up target 30% above current load).

Rollback procedure (when to and how):
- When: Any canary wave fails model-quality threshold (BLEU/ROUGE analogs for evals, or customer prompt tests) or latency breaches SLOs in restored paths.
- How (steps):
  1) routing-orchestrator sets model route back to previous model variant.
  2) Drain refreshed nodes: send SIGTERM and wait for in-flight tokens to complete (grace period 90s).
  3) Rebuild KV-cache on previous variant if necessary from preserved snapshots.
  4) Publish a rollback event including metrics snapshot and annotated errors.

Verification and postmortem checklist (post-failover):
- Verify p95/p99 RTT stabilizes under configured thresholds for 30m.
- Confirm KV-cache hit-rate for warmed models is >80% within 10 minutes of promotion.
- Run a predefined customer prompt set (10 prompts) and compare outputs to baseline quality; record regression scores.
- If rollback occurred, ensure artifact attestation and signed image manifests are preserved per compliance: save manifest to /evidence/rollback/<tenant>/<timestamp>.json.

Monitoring, alerts and dashboards:
- Metric collection: control_plane_rtt_p50/p95/p99, egress_error_rate, cache_hit_rate, model_swap_success_rate.
- Dashboards: Tenant-level latency heatmap, KV-cache warm progress, active routing policy map.
- Alerts (examples):
  - P99 RTT > 350ms for 30s -> SEV3 oncall notify + routing-orchestrator check (runbook link in alert).
  - Request failure rate > 5% for 5m -> SEV2 with automated degraded routing (if configured).

Preflight (deployment) checklist for customers and field teams:
- Ensure local-runtime has at least 20% spare GPU capacity reserved for standby warmups.
- Control-plane-proxy TLS cert rotation scheduled and verified.
- routing-orchestrator has IAM service account with scoped permissions: metrics:read, routing:update, runtime:invoke.
- Define per-tenant routing-policy YAML and upload to control plane; minimum fields: allowed_variants, warm_models, degradation_priority.

Sample routing-policy YAML (minimal):

apiVersion: redwood.io/v1
kind: RoutingPolicy
metadata:
  tenant: tenant-123
spec:
  allowed_variants:
    - id: default
      priority: 100
    - id: quantized-8bit
      priority: 80
  warm_models:
    - model-id: rwd-gpt-13b
      top_k: 5
  degradation_priority:
    - route: non-critical-chat
      actions: [quantize, rate-limit]

CLI snippets (operator):
- Trigger KV-cache warm manually:
  export LOCAL_OP_TOKEN=...
  curl -X POST https://local-runtime.example.internal/v1/warm 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOCAL_OP_TOKEN" 
    -d '{"models":["rwd-gpt-13b","rwd-embed-2"], "samples": 20}'

- Inspect routing policy applied to a tenant (kubectl example for hosted operator):
  kubectl -n redwood get routingpolicy tenant-123 -o yaml

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments SRE (team alias: eng-pd-sre).
- Oncall: eng-sre rotation (channel: #oncall-redwood-pd).
- Escalation path: operator -> field SE -> eng-pd-sre -> infra-sre -> product-eng if needed.

Safety and cost controls:
- All automatic fallbacks must obey per-tenant cost ceilings configured in control plane. If fallback would exceed the tenant ceiling, routing-orchestrator will open a human approval request and reduce traffic rather than fail open.

Appendix A — sample incident timeline (example):
- 2026-02-14 10:02 UTC: p99 RTT climbs to 370ms (60s window) -> Stage 1 watch triggered.
- 10:04: routing-orchestrator triggers KV-cache warm for top-3 models.
- 10:06: cache_hit_rate improved to 62% for rwd-gpt-13b.
- 10:10: p99 still > 350ms -> Stage 2 degrade activated, routing updated to prefer quantized variants for non-critical routes.
- 10:28: sustained packet loss observed -> Stage 3 failover activated to regional-fallback; tickets and customer-notify email sent.
